2900:

Berl. Akad.” 80.22, “Supp.epigram” 2.829 (Damascus, 3rd c.AD)}}; ἐν χειρὶ κ. with a **mighty** hand, {{LXX+2nd c.BC+|LXX.Exo.13.3, +others; κ. ἀγών 2nd c.BC: Polybius Historicus 2.69.8; τόξα κ. 1st-2nd c.AD: Plutarchus Biographus et Philosophus “Crassus” 24; ἐπὶ τὸ κ. 2nd c.AD: Lucianus Sophista “Anach.” 28}}: _comparative_, {{Refs 1st c.AD+|1st c.AD: Philo Judaeus 1.14}}: _superlative_, {{Refs|[prev. author] 2.383}}; especially in magical and mystical writings, ἐν φωτὶ κ. καὶ ἀφθάρτῳ {{Refs|“PMag.Lond.” 121.563; θεοὶ κ. 2903:
** κρᾰτιστ-ος**, η, ον,
_Epic dialect_ **κάρτ-** (as always in {{Refs 8th c.BC+|8th c.BC: Homerus Epicus), isolated Superl. from κρατύς}}, **strongest, mightiest**, {{Refs 8th c.BC+|8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 1.266, etc.; θεῶν κ., i.e. Zeus. 5th c.BC: Pindarus Lyricus “O.” 14.13; κ. Ἑλλήνων, i.e. Achilles, 5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Ph.” 3: in Prose, εἰ τοὺς κ. ἐνικήσαμεν 5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 7.67}}; Λημνίων τὸ κ. **the best** of their men, {{Refs|[prev\. author] 5.8; τὸ δυνάμεως κ.}} **the strength** or **flower** of.., {{Refs 5th c.BC+|5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Cyr.” 6.1.28}}, etc.; of things, καρτίστην.. μάχην **fiercest** fight, {{Refs 8th c.BC+|8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 6.185; δεσμὸς κ. Ti.Locrian dialect 99a}}.
**2** generally, **best, most excellent**, as _superlative_ of ἀγαθός, [{{Refs 5th c.BC+|5th c.BC: Pindarus Lyricus “I.” 1.17, 5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Ant.” 1050, etc.: colloquially, ἄνδρα κ. εἰπών Theophrastus Philosophus [{4-3rd c.BC}] “Characteres” 5.2}}]; οἱ κράτιστοι **the aristocracy**, [{{Refs 5th c.BC+|5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “HG” 7.1.42, see at {ἀγαθός} 1; τὰ κ. τῆς χώρας [prev. work] 3.4.20.}}]
**2.b** as a title or mode of address, {{NT|κράτιστε Θεόφιλε NT.Luke.1.3}}; especially = Latin _egregius_, {{Refs 1st c.AD+|ὁ κ. ἡγεμών “PFay.” p.33 (1st c.AD); ὁ κ. ἐπίτροπος “BGU” 891 (2nd c.AD); ἡ κ.}}, of a woman of the **equester ordo,** {{Refs|Inscriptiones Graecae 14. 1346; also, =}} Latin _clarissimus_, of Senators, ὁ κ. ἀνθὐπατος {{Refs 3rd c.AD+|[prev. work]9(1).61; ὁ κ. συγκλητικός “IGRom.” 3.581, etc.; ἡ κ. βουλή “POxy.” 2108.6 (3rd c.AD).}}
**2.c** with modal words added, {{Refs 5th c.BC+|κ. τὴν ψυχήν 5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 2.40}}; πάντων πάντα κ. **best** of all in.., [{{Refs 6th c.BC+|5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “An.” 1.9.2; ἔν τινι [prev\. author] “Mem.” 3.4.5; εἴς τι Plato Philosophus [{5-6th c.BC}] “Philebus” 67b; περί τι [prev\. author] “Plt.” 257a; πρός τι Xenophon Historicus [{5-6th c.BC}] “Historia Graeca (Hellenica)” 3.4.16}}]: with _infinitive_, **best at** doing, {{Refs 5th c.BC+|5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 2.81, 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Phdr.” 267d, 5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Mem.” 1.4.1}}, etc.: with _participle_, {{Refs|τῶν ἡλίκων κ. εἶναι ἀκοντίζων καὶ τοξεύων [prev\. author] “Cyr.” 1.3.15}}.
**3** _neuter_ followed by _infinitive_, φυγέειν κάρτιστον to flee were **best**, {{Refs 8th c.BC+|8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 12.120, compare 5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “El.” 379, 5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Eq.” 80, etc.: in _plural_, κράτιστα.. ἑλεῖν 5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Med.” 384}}: _absolutely_, ὅπερ κ. the **main point**, {{Refs 5th c.BC+|5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 1.143.}}
**4** _adverb_ usages, ἀπὸ τοῦ κρατίστου **in all good faith**, {{Refs 2nd c.BC+|2nd c.BC: Polybius Historicus 8.17.4; κατὰ τὸ κ. 1st c.BC: Dionysius Halicarnassensis 2.22}}: _neuter_ _plural_ κράτιστα as _adverb_, {{Refs 5th c.BC+|5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “HG” 3.4.16, “Ages.” 1.25.}} —The _comparative_ in use is κρείσσων (which see).
2905:
** κραυγ-άζω**,
={κράζω}, of dogs, **bay,** {{Refs|Lyric poetry Adesp. 135}}; of ravens, **croak**, {{Refs 2nd c.AD+|2nd c.AD: Arrianus Historicus “Epict.” 3.1.37}}; of men, **cry aloud, shout**, {{NT+4th c.BC+|4th c.BC: Demosthenes Orator 54.7, LXX.2Esd.3.13, “NT.John.18.40”, 1st-2nd c.AD: Polemo Sophista “Cyn.” 40, 2nd c.AD: Galenus Medicus 8.287; κ. μὴ θυμοῦ” 1st c.BC: Philodemus Gadarensis Epigrammaticus “Ir.” p.70 W.; κραυγάζω κοὐκ ἐπακούει “Riv.Fil.” 57.380 (from Aptera).}}
2906:
** κραυγ-ή**, ἡ,
**crying, screaming, shouting**, τίς ἥδε κ.; [{{Refs 6th c.BC+|5th c.BC: Teleclides Comicus 35; κραυγὴν θεῖναι, στῆσαι, 5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Or.” 1510, 1529; ποιεῖν Xenophon Historicus [{5-6th c.BC}] “Institutio Cyri (Cyropaedia)” 3.1.4; κραυγῇ χρῆσθαι 5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 2.4; κ. γίγνεται 5th c.BC: Lysias Orator 13.71}}]; rarely of a **shout of joy,** {{NT+5th c.BC+|PPetr. 3p.334 (3rd c.BC), NT.Luke.1.42: in _plural_, 4th c.BC: Aeschines Orator 1.34, 2nd c.AD: Vettius Valens Astrologus 2.35; κραυγὴ Καλλιόπης, as an instance of bad taste, cited from. 5th c.BC: Dionysius Chalcus Elegiacus (7) by 4th c.BC: Aristoteles Philosophus “Rh.” 1405a33.}}
2908:
** κρείσσων**, ον,
_genitive_ ονος, as always in _Epic dialect_ and old _Attic dialect_; later _Attic dialect_ **κρείττων**; _Ionic dialect_ **κρέσσων** {{Refs 5th c.BC+|5th c.BC: Hippocrates Medicus “Fract.” 3, +others, variant in 4th c.BC: Dionysius Tragicus (see. below 11); _Doric dialect_}} **κάρρων** (which see); Cretan dialect **κάρτων** {{Refs|“Leg.Gort.” 1.15:}} — _comparative_ of κρατύς (see. κράτιστος), **stronger, mightier**, {{Refs 8th c.BC+|κ. βασιλεύς, ὅτε χώσεται ἀνδρὶ χέρηϊ 8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 1.80}}; especially in battle, [{{Refs 6th c.BC+|κρείσσοσιν ἶφι μάχεσθαι 21.486; Διὸς κ. νόος ἠέ περ ἀνδρῶν 16.688; κεραυνοῦ κρέσσον.. βέλος 5th c.BC: Pindarus Lyricus “I.” 8(7).36, compare 5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 7.172, Hp.[same place], etc.; κρείσσων χεῖρας 5th c.BC: Antipho Orator 4.4.7; τὸ τοῦ κ. συμφέρον Plato Philosophus [{5-6th c.BC}] “Respublica” 338c, compare 3rd c.AD: Democritus Epigrammaticus 267}}]: hence, **having the upper hand, superior**, {{Refs 8th c.BC+|ὁππότερος δέ κε νικήσῃ κ. τε γένηται 8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 3.71; κ. ἀρετῇ τε βίῃ τε 23.578}}: as Law-term, of witnesses, {{Refs|κάρτονανς ἦμεν _prevail,_ Leges Gortynensium}} [prev. cited]
**2** frequently as _comparative_ of ἀγαθός, **better**, κρέσσονες one's **betters**, especially in point of rank, {{Refs 5th c.BC+|5th c.BC: Pindarus Lyricus “O.” 10(11).39, “N.” 10.72 (but also, _the stronger, more powerful_, 5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Or.” 710, 5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 1.8, etc.); ἐς τοὺς τοκέας καὶ ἐς τοὺς κρέσσονας τεθυμῶσθαι 5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 3.52, compare “SIG” 685.134 (5th c.BC: Magnes Comicus Mae., 2nd c.BC); οἱ κ. corps of guards at Thebes, 1st-2nd c.AD: Plutarchus Biographus et Philosophus 2.598e; κρείσσονες θεοί}}, of the **greater** gods, as opposed to to Oceanus, {{Refs 4th c.BC+|4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus “Pr.” 902 (Lyric poetry); ὁ κ. Ζεύς [prev\. author] “Ag.” 60}} (_anapaest meter_); οἱ κ. the **Higher Powers**, [{{Refs 5th c.BC+|[prev\. author] “fragment” 10, 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Sph.” 216b, “Euthd.” 291a, etc.; τὰ κρείσσω, ={τὰ θεῖα}, 5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Ion” 973; τὸ κ.}}] the **Almighty, Providence,** {{Refs 4th c.AD+|Corp.Herm. 18.11, 4th c.AD: Julianus Imperator “Ep.” 204, 6th c.AD: Agathias Historicus et Epigrammaticus 1.16, 5th-6th c.AD: Procopius Gazaeus Rhetor “Pan.” p.492; τὰ κρείσσονα}} one's **advantages**, {{Refs 5th c.BC+|τὰ ὑπάρχοντα ἡμῖν κρείσσω καταπροδοῦναι 5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 4.10}}.
**3** with _infinitive_, οὔ τις ἐμεῖο κρείσσων.. δόμεναι no one has **a better right** to.., [{{Refs 8th c.BC+|8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 21.345; οὐκ ἄλλος κ. παραμυθεῖσθαι Plato Philosophus [{5-6th c.BC}] “Politicus” 268b}}]; κρεῖσσόν ἐστι with _infinitive_, 'tis **better** to.., [{{Refs 5th c.BC+|κ. γάρ ἐστιν εἰσάπαξ θανεῖν ἢ.. πάσχειν κακῶς Aeschylus Tragicus [{4-5th c.BC}] “Prometheus Vinctus” 750, compare 624, 5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 3.52, etc.; τὸ μὴ εἶναι κ. ἢ τὸ ζῆν κακῶς 5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “fragment” 488, compare 4th-3rd c.BC: Apollodorus Comicus 6; also κρείσσων εἰμί}}] with _participle_, κ. γὰρ ἦσθα μηκέτ᾽ ὢν ἢ ζῶν τυφλός thou wert **better** not alive, than living blind, {{Refs 5th c.BC+|5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “OT” 1368, compare “Aj.” 635 (Lyric poetry); κ. ἦν ὁ ἀγὼν μὴ γεγενημένος 4th c.BC: Aeschines Orator 1.192, compare 1st c.BC: Dionysius Halicarnassensis 6.9.}}
**II** with _genitive_ or ἤ, **too great for, surpassing, beyond**, [{{Refs 5th c.BC+|ὕψος κ. ἐκπηδήματος Aeschylus Tragicus [{4-5th c.BC}] “Agamemnon” 1376}}]; of evil deeds, κρείσσον᾽ ἀγχόνης **too bad** for hanging, {{Refs 5th c.BC+|5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “OT” 1374; κρεῖσσον δεργμάτων}} **too bad** to look on, {{Refs 5th c.BC+|5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Hipp.” 1217; θαυμάτων [prev\. author] “Ba.” 667}}; λέγετι σιγῆς κρεῖσσον {{Refs 5th c.BC+|(κρέσσον “PSI” 9.1093) ἢ σιγὴν ἔχε 4th c.BC: Dionysius Tragicus 6; κρείσσον᾽ ἢ λέξαι λόγῳ τολμήματα 5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Supplices” 844}}; κ. ἢ λόγοισιν (i.e. εἰπεῖν) {{Refs|[prev\. author] “IT” 837; ἀναρχία κ. πυρός [prev\. author] “Hec.” 608}}; πρᾶγμα ἐλπίδος κ. γεγενημένον **worse** than one expected, [{{Refs 6th c.BC+|5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 2.64; κ. λόγου τὸ κάλλος Xenophon Historicus [{5-6th c.BC}] “Memorabilia” 3.11.1; κ. τῆς ἡμετέρας δυνάμεως [prev\. author] “Cyr.” 7.5.9}}].
**III** **having control over, master of**, especially of desires and passions, [{{Refs 6th c.BC+|τῶν ἡδονῶν 3rd c.AD: Democritus Epigrammaticus 214; τοῦ ἔρωτος Xenophon Historicus [{5-6th c.BC}] “Institutio Cyri (Cyropaedia)” 6.1.34}}]; γαστρὸς καὶ κερδέων {{Refs|[prev. work] 4.2.45; αὑτῶν}} **over** themselves, {{Refs 5th c.BC+|5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Phdr.” 232a, +others; κ. χρημάτων}} **superior to** the influence of money, [{{Refs 6th c.BC+|5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 2.60, 5th-6th c.BC: Isocrates Orator 1.19; τῶν συμμάχων κ. Xenophon Historicus [{5-6th c.BC}] “Respublica Atheniensium” 2.1}}]; also, **putting oneself above**, {{Refs 5th c.BC+|κ. τοῦ δικαίου 5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 3.84}}; κρείσσους ὄντες.. τῷ λογισμῷ ἐς τὸ ἀνέλπιστον τοῦ βεβαίου having reasoned themselves into an absolute belief of the hopelessness of certainty, [{{Refs 4th c.BC+|[prev. work] 83; φαύλους καὶ κρείττους τῆς παιδείας, ={οὓς παιδευθῆναι ἀδύνατον} (just below), 4th c.BC: Aristoteles Philosophus “Pol.” 1316a9.}}]
**IV** **better, more excellent**, {{Refs 1st c.AD+|ἁρμονίη ἀφανὴς φανερῆς κ. 1st c.AD: Heraclitus 54; κ. ἐπ᾽ ἀρετήν 3rd c.AD: Democritus Epigrammaticus 181}}; ὁ κρείττων λόγος (opposed to ὁ ἥσσων) {{Refs 5th c.BC+|5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Nu.” 113; κατὰ τὸ κ.}} in a **higher** sense, opposed to κατὰ τὸ χεῖρον, {{Refs 5th c.AD+|5th-6th c.AD: Damascius Philosophus “Pr.” 7.}}
**V** _adverb_ {{Refs 5th c.BC+|κρεισσόνως 5th c.BC: Antipho Orator 4.4.6, 4th c.AD: Iamblichus Philosophus “Myst.” 7.4; also κρεῖσσον 5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Oedipus Tyrannus” 176 (Lyric poetry), “OGI” 90.31 (Rosetta, 2nd c.BC). (κρέσσων from κρέτ-yων, compare κρέτο; κάρτων and κάρρων from κάρτ-yων, compare κάρτο; κρείσσων (like μείζων)}} probably took ει from ὀλείζων.)
